## Shift models (observed = db(air) + shift)

Per-segment linear fit `obs−db = a + b·(λ−λ0)` from isolated strong sample-element I/II anchors (UV, VIS) + isolated Ar I lines (NIR), sub-pixel parabolic centroid, on the fresh pool. The wavelength shift is an INSTRUMENT property (element-independent); the ambient Ar I lines are textbook wavelength standards and give a clean seed, so element anchors farther than 0.13 nm from the Ar seed (dense-spectrum centroids that snapped to a neighbour) are rejected.

After the PIXEL_OFFSET −18 fix the residual shift is small: Fe pool **-20 pm**, V pool **-43 pm** (both tens of pm, vs the −152/−158 pm of the superseded −18 px analysis). The two metals now agree to ~22 pm, consistent with an element-independent instrument shift; the previously reported ‘V line list carries an extra ~150 pm offset’ was an artefact of the −18 px axis interacting with the V-anchor selection — the residual V-vs-Fe difference is now a few tens of pm, not 150 pm (its effect on completeness is quantified in §1.4).

### 1.4 Matched fraction vs matching tolerance (db wavelength accuracy)

Fraction of peaks with ANY sample-element I/II db line within ±tol of the shift-corrected position. If a metal needs a wider tolerance to reach the same fraction, its db air wavelengths are less accurate (not that lines are missing).

**Verdict — do all observed lines match?** 
To ±0.15 nm, 86% of Fe peaks and 78% of V peaks match a sample-element line; at ±0.40 nm this rises to 95% (Fe) and 88% (V). On the corrected axis both curves are much higher at ±0.15 nm than in the superseded report (Fe 83→86%, V 59→78%): with the −18 px error removed, peaks land within a pitch of their db positions. Fe is nearly saturated by ±0.15 nm; V still lags Fe by ~8 points at ±0.15 nm and closes the gap only near ±0.40 nm, so the V I/II line list's air wavelengths remain modestly less accurate than Fe's — but the large ‘extra V offset’ of the −18 px analysis is gone. Once db wavelength accuracy is accounted for, essentially all strong observed lines DO match the sample element (plus ambient Ar/O/N/H and, in a 99.98% Fe / pure-V matrix, no established bulk impurity); the residual unmatched at ±0.15 nm is dominated by db wavelength error (V) and NIR ambient bands, not by unidentified emission. Confidence: high for Fe UV/VIS, moderate for V and for both NIR (ambient-dominated, weak shift constraint).

## 2. How much self-absorption?

### 2a. Multiplet / doublet ratio test → τ

Isolated same-upper-level (branching, T-independent) or same-lower-level (resonance) pairs of COMPARABLE strength: same ion, same segment, 0.25<|Δλ|<8 nm, exact shared level, thin ratio R₀∈[1.2,4], absorption-strength ratio sr∈[0.3,4], both SNR≥12. Thin emission ratio R₀ ∝ (gA/λ)·e^(−Eₖ/kT); optical-depth ratio sr ∝ gA·λ²·e^(−Eᵢ/kT). τ from `invert_doublet_tau(R, R₀, sr)` (escape factor (1−e^−τ)/τ). Deviation of the measured ratio R toward 1 = optical depth. SA can only push R toward 1 from above, so pairs with R<1 (a forest-contaminated weak member) are rejected and counted.

### 2b. Boltzmann deficit of the resonance lines

A robust Boltzmann reference ln(area·λ/gA) vs Eₖ is fit over non-resonance isolated stage lines (Eᵢ≥0.8 eV, iterative 1.8σ rejection). Its rms is the single-line noise floor (db gA error + blends + baseline); only a deficit well above it is significant. The resonance / low-Eᵢ lines (Eᵢ<0.6 eV) are then read against it: a systematic deficit r (ln units, loss 1−eʳ) is self-absorption. (Non-resonance outliers with huge deficits are mismeasured lines, not SA, and are excluded.)

**Fe 1** (360–560 nm): reference from 35 non-resonance lines, noise floor rms 0.32 ln (significance threshold |r|>0.6); reference slope-T 12498 K is ill-constrained by this scatter and is not used as a thermometer. Resonance / low-Eᵢ lines (Eᵢ<0.6 eV):

### 2e. Reconciliation

- **V shows self-absorption on its strong comparable-strength multiplets.** On the corrected axis the multiplet-ratio test selects 7 usable V pairs; the strongest are 565.74/560.49 (τ≈3.5), 653.14/645.23 (τ≈1.4), 609.02/603.97 (τ≈1.4) — SA correction factors ~1.8–3.6× if pairs exist. The Boltzmann deficit independently flags 8/14 resonance/low-Eᵢ V I lines sitting well below the thin reference. NB: the specific V I 417.94/415.97 and 478.65/475.39 pairs highlighted in the superseded report are NOT among the comparable-strength isolated pairs selected here on the corrected axis; the dedicated ePSF measurement put 417.94/415.97 at τ≈2.10 [1.99, 2.18] vs 2.05 thin (a small, real SA), so the qualitative ‘V has moderate SA’ conclusion holds while the exact lines and τ values change.

- **Fe now also shows self-absorption on a few clean pairs** (τ_strong>0.3 on 3 Fe pairs, e.g. 589.80/589.53 (τ≈8.5), 357.01/364.78 (τ≈2.3), 296.69/293.69 (τ≈1.2)), where the superseded −18 px analysis found the surviving Fe pairs optically thin (τ≈0). Fe's dense line forest still leaves few clean comparable pairs and the single-line Boltzmann scatter (rms ~0.3 ln) is large, so most Fe SA is read from the Boltzmann deficit (1/4 low-Eᵢ lines) rather than pairs. Fe I 438.35 remains a self-absorbed low-lier in the companion Fe study.

- **Width shows no opacity broadening at this resolution** (§2c): FWHM vs log-area slope is ≈0 / slightly negative for both metals, so SA compresses line AREA without measurably broadening the ~2–3-pixel instrumental profile. SA therefore biases Boltzmann T upward (strong low-Eᵢ lines lost) and would bias any composition-type intensity of the affected V resonance lines low by the correction factors above.

## 3. How much broadening, and which mechanisms?

FWHM: Gaussian fit over peak ±3 native samples (baseline-subtracted), isolated lines SNR≥10 per segment. Instrumental = 15th-percentile lower envelope per segment + Ar I NIR lines. Doppler at T=9 kK. Stark/opacity = excess width over instrumental (Gaussian-subtraction upper bound; Voigt caveat noted).

### 3.4 Decomposition

- **Instrumental** dominates. The lower-envelope FWHM is 1.3/1.1/1.5 px (Fe) and 1.4/1.0/1.3 px (V) for UV/VIS/NIR — i.e. ~115/146/266 pm (Fe), ~124/127/236 pm (V), matching the cool Ar I NIR purge lines, which have negligible Stark — resolution ~1.1–1.5 px per segment.

- **Doppler** is a few pm at 9 kK (2.7–6.9 pm Fe, 2.9–7.2 pm V; §3.1), ≥20× below a native pixel — undetectable here.

- **Stark** is bounded, not measured. The clean-line median VIS width is only ~1.0–1.5× instrumental and it does not fall with delay (§3.3: 186→174 pm (Fe, delay 5→20 µs), 177→178 pm (V, delay 5→50 µs), within the replicate SD) — if Stark were significant the width would shrink as nₑ decays. So the Stark+Doppler excess over instrumental is an UPPER bound on nₑ broadening; no Stark width parameter for these Fe I/V I lines is cited with confidence, so it is not converted to an nₑ value (Hα is unusable — weak/blended here).

- **Self-absorption / opacity broadening** is marginal at this resolution: a few strong lines (§3.2) exceed the instrumental width but several are blends (large Δpos), and the width–area slope (§2c) is flat-to-negative — SA compresses line AREA far more than it broadens the instrument-limited profile.

| peaks SNR≥5 | 371 | 388 |

| typical τ_strong (SA pairs) | 2.29 | 1.38 |

| VIS median FWHM (nm) | 175 pm | 158 pm |
| usable isolated lines (SNR≥10) | 75 | 71 |
| atomic mass (u) | 55.845 | 50.942 |

**Physical differences.** Fe I/II is far denser (2,526 Fe I + 6,463 Fe II db lines vs 1,161 V I + 1,767 V II), so more Fe peaks are blends. On the corrected axis both metals match far better (§1.4): Fe saturates by ±0.15 nm and V now reaches 78% at ±0.15 nm (vs 59% before the fix), lagging Fe by only ~8 points — the V line list's air wavelengths still scatter somewhat more than Fe's, but the large ‘extra V offset’ was an axis artefact, not db error. Self-absorption is measurable on V's strong comparable-strength multiplets (τ up to ~3.5; the dedicated ePSF measurement puts V I 417.94/415.97 at τ≈2.10) and now on a few Fe pairs too, though Fe SA is mostly read from the Boltzmann deficit. V II 309.3/310.2/311.1 is UV, where response and SNR limit the diagnostics. Fe (56 u) and V (51 u) differ <10% in mass, so Doppler widths are within ~5%, and both share the same three-segment spectrometer (resolution ~1.1–1.5 px) — the differences are line density, resonance-line strength and residual V-db wavelength accuracy, not optics. Implication for calibration: Fe is ready for quantitative line work now; V benefits from a modest per-segment line-list re-registration and SA correction on its resonance multiplets.

## Limits and unverified

- **Segment response is uncorrected.** Multiplet ratios are restricted to one segment and ≤8 nm to keep the response ≈flat; cross-segment intensity comparisons are not made. R₀ uses an energy-emissivity convention (∝gA/λ); a photon convention would shift R₀ by λ ratios (~5% over 20 nm).

- **τ from a homogeneous-slab escape factor** (`alibz.utils.absorption`); real plasmas have gradients, so τ is a lower bound on the peak optical depth and the SA correction is a slab-average.

- **Stark → nₑ not converted.** No Stark width parameter for these specific Fe I / V I lines is cited from memory with confidence, so the excess width is reported as an upper bound on Stark+Doppler+opacity only; Hα is unusable (blended/weak here). Gaussian-quadrature width subtraction over-subtracts for a Lorentzian (Stark) core, so the excess is an upper bound.

- **Shift scatter** (σ per model above) is ~0.5–1 native pitch; a peak within ±0.15 nm can match the wrong member of a close db multiplet, so "matched-unique" is a resolution-limited statement, not a line-ID proof.

- V "fresh pool" mixes 12 raster sites and 3 delays; the best-run tables use the single highest-score 10/10 replicate only.
